cases.request: اكتب قصيدة نثر من خمسة أسطر عن مفتاح بقي في جيب معطف بعد انتقال صاحبه إلى بيت جديد. بلغة يومية هادئة، ومن غير موعظة أو شرح بعد القصيدة.
cases.response:
في البيت الجديد، علّقتُ المعطف خلف الباب.  
بقي المفتاح القديم في جيبه، مع إيصال مطويّ.  
كلما بحثتُ عن نقود، لمستُ أسنانه بأصابعي.  
هذا الصباح أخرجتُه، ووقفتُ قليلًا قرب الصناديق.  
ثم أعدتُه إلى الجيب، وسوّيتُ ياقة المعطف.

cases.request: اشرح الصورة في هذا النص من غير إعادة كتابته: «كل مساء أترك الكرسي قبالة الباب، وأرفع عن المقعد غبار يوم آخر». هل يثبت النص أن الغائب مات؟
cases.response:
**لا، النص لا يثبت أن الغائب مات.** إنه يوحي بالانتظار واستمرار الغياب، لكنه لا يحدد سببه.

«كل مساء» تجعل الفعل طقسًا متكررًا؛ فالانتظار يتجدد يومًا بعد يوم. ووجود الكرسي «قبالة الباب» يربطه بإمكان الدخول والعودة، فيغدو المقعد مكانًا محفوظًا لشخص يُنتظر حضوره.

وفي «غبار يوم آخر» يتحول مرور الزمن إلى أثر مادي يمكن مسحه. رفع الغبار قد يوحي بإبقاء المكان مهيّأً للعودة، أو بمقاومة تراكم الغياب والنسيان. وتضيف كلمة «آخر» إحساسًا بثقل الأيام المتشابهة.

يمكن قراءة المشهد بوصفه وفاءً لميت، لكن يمكن أيضًا قراءته انتظارًا لمسافر أو مفارق. **الموت احتمال تأويلي، لا واقعة يقررها النص.**

cases.request: Explain in English which meter this verse fits, show one compact supporting scan, and distinguish its rhyme letter from its final pronounced sound. Keep this in chat; no editor. قِفَا نَبْكِ مِنْ ذِكْرَى حَبِيبٍ وَمَنْزِلِ * بِسِقْطِ اللِّوَى بَيْنَ الدَّخُولِ فَحَوْمَلِ
cases.response:
The verse fits **al-Ṭawīl (البحر الطويل)**. The local scanner confirms that both halves fit, with the final kasra lengthened to **ī** in metrical recitation.

Here is a complete scan of the first half. **ب** means a short syllable; **−** means a long one. Read each pattern in the displayed order.

| Pronounced group (metrical spelling) | Syllables | Foot |
|---|---|---|
| قِفَا نَبْ | ب − − | فعولن |
| كِ مِنْ ذِكْرَى | ب − − − | مفاعيلن |
| حَبِيبِنْ | ب − − | فعولن |
| وَمَنْزِلِي | ب − ب − | مفاعلن |

Foot boundaries can divide words: **نَبْكِ** crosses the first boundary. The second half also fits, using the permitted shortened foot **فعولُ** in its third position.

The **rhyme letter (الروي) is ل**, the *l* in **فَحَوْمَلِ**. The final pronounced sound in this recitation is **ī**, giving *fa-ḥawmalī*. That lengthened vowel is **وصل**, conventionally represented as a supplementary yāʾ; it is **not** the rhyme letter.

cases.request: ما البحر المحتمل لعبارة «يا قلب لا تسأل عن الغائبين»؟ أريد جوابًا أوليًا مختصرًا. ليست عندي بقية القصيدة ولا تسجيل للإلقاء.
cases.response:
الأقرب مبدئيًا **بحر السريع**، بافتراض القراءة: «يَا قَلْبُ لَا تَسْأَلْ عَنِ الْغَائِبِينْ»، مع وصل الكلمات والوقف على النون.

يؤيد الفحص المحلي هذا التقطيع؛ والمجموعات كتابة عروضية بحسب النطق:

| المجموعة | المقاطع | التفعيلة |
|---|---|---|
| يَا قَلْبُ لَا | − − ب − | مستفعلن |
| تَسْأَلْ عَنِلْ | − − ب − | مستفعلن |
| غَائِبِينْ | − ب = | فاعلانْ |

«ب» قصير، و«−» طويل، و«=» مديد عند الوقف. هذا **ترجيح للعبارة وحدها**، وليس حكمًا قاطعًا على بحر القصيدة.

cases.request: هذا تمرين وزني: «قَرِيبٌ صَدِيقِي بَعِيدٌ جِدًّا مَكَانِي». أريد أربع تفعيلات فعولن بلا زحاف. أصلحه بأقل تغيير، واحتفظ بكلمات قريب وصديقي وبعيد ومكاني. بيّن أثر التغيير في المعنى وأرني دليل الوزن قبل التغيير وبعده. التشكيل المعطى هو قراءتي المقصودة.
cases.response:
**قَرِيبٌ صَدِيقِي بَعِيدٌ مَكَانِي**

أقلّ تغيير هو حذف **«جِدًّا»** وحدها؛ تبقى الكلمات الأربع بترتيبها وتشكيلها. يبقى قرب الصديق وبُعد المكان، لكن تزول المبالغة في شدة البُعد.

التقطيع على وصل الكلمات، وفق قراءتك المعطاة: **ب** مقطع قصير، و**−** مقطع طويل. نفكّ التنوين والشدة في الكتابة العروضية:

| اللفظ عروضِيًّا | المقاطع | الوزن |
|---|---|---|
| قَرِيبُنْ | قَ / رِي / بُنْ | ب − − = فعولن |
| صَدِيقِي | صَ / دِي / قِي | ب − − = فعولن |
| بَعِيدُنْ | بَ / عِي / دُنْ | ب − − = فعولن |
| جِدْدَنْ | جِدْ / دَنْ | − − : زيادة ✗ |
| مَكَانِي | مَ / كَا / نِي | ب − − = فعولن |

**قبل التغيير:**  
ب − − ⁞ ب − − ⁞ ب − − ⁞ **− − ✗** ⁞ ب − −

**بعد التغيير:**  
ب − − ⁞ ب − − ⁞ ب − − ⁞ ب − −  
**فعولن ⁞ فعولن ⁞ فعولن ⁞ فعولن**

إذن «جِدًّا» تزيد مقطعين طويلين؛ بحذفها تتحقق أربع تفعيلات سليمة، بلا زحاف أو تغيير في النطق. تحققتُ من الأصل والتعديل بالمقطّع المحلي.

حفظتُ [الأصل](original.txt) و[التعديل المقترح](proposal.txt) منفصلين. لم أفتح محرّر ديوان لعدم توفر عارض محلي.

cases.request:
أقرأ هذا النص موصولًا مع نطق نون التنوين: «يَدٌ
تَاهَتْ». هل يصح وصفه بأنه تفعيلة كامل سليمة؟ افحص هذه القراءة نفسها ولا تغيّر الألفاظ أو تسقط التنوين.
cases.response:
لا، **لا يصح وصف هذه القراءة بأنها تفعيلة كامل سليمة**. مع الوصل وإثبات نون التنوين تكون الكتابة العروضية: **«يَدُنْ تَاهَتْ»**.

| المقاطع المنطوقة بالترتيب | يَ | دُنْ | تَا | هَتْ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| الوزن | ب | − | − | − |

«ب» مقطع قصير، و«−» مقطع طويل. فوزن النص **ب − − −**، بينما تفعيلة الكامل السليمة **متَفاعلن: ب ب − ب −**؛ فلا يتطابقان. وأكّد الفاحص المحلي هذا الاختلال عند اختبار القراءة نفسها على الكامل.

فاصل السطر لا يغيّر النتيجة مع الوصل الذي حدّدته؛ نون التنوين منطوقة ومحسوبة، ولا يجوز إسقاطها للحصول على وزن آخر.

# شعر التفعيلة والشعر الحر

## Definitions
- **شعر التفعيلة** (often called الشعر الحر in Arabic criticism since نازك الملائكة
  and بدر شاكر السياب, late 1940s): the line (السطر) is built from **one repeated
  taf'ila**, but the number of feet per line is free and lines need not rhyme
  regularly.
- **قصيدة النثر**: not bound to a Khalilian meter. Identify the intended form
  from the request and text; a failed scanner match alone cannot classify it. It is a poetic form, not a failed attempt at meter.
- Some poets mix taf'ilas from one "circle" (e.g. مستفعلن with فاعلن as in
  البسيط) — the scanner handles one family at a time; mention mixed usage when
  two families each fit different stretches.

## Taf'ila families (the "صافية" meters used in free verse)

These are the implementation's supported families, not a complete taxonomy of modern Arabic rhythm. The shared المتدارك/الخبب label is an implementation convention; keep theoretical distinctions visible when relevant. See [coverage and sources](SCANNER-SOURCES.md).
| التفعيلة | البحر | صور الحشو | نهايات السطر الشائعة |
|---|---|---|---|
| متفاعلن | الكامل | متَفاعلن ب ب − ب −، متْفاعلن − − ب − | متفاعلْ، متفاعلانْ، متفاعلاتن، فعِلن |
| مستفعلن | الرجز | مستفعلن، متفعلن، مستعلن | مستفعلْ، متفعلْ، مستفعلانْ |
| فاعلاتن | الرمل | فاعلاتن، فعِلاتن | فاعلانْ، فاعلن، فعِلن، فاعلاتانْ |
| فعولن | المتقارب | فعولن، فعولُ | فعولْ، فعو، فعْ |
| فاعلن | المتدارك/الخبب | فاعلن، فعِلن، فعْلن | فاعلانْ، فاعلاتن |
| مفاعيلن | الهزج | مفاعيلن، مفاعيلُ | فعولن |
| مفاعلتن | الوافر | مفاعلتن، مفاعلْتن | فعولن |

## Rules the scanner applies
- A scanned sequence uses the supported feet; a foot may cross a printed
  line break. Implemented line-ending forms may apply where the reading and
  intended convention permit them.
- **التدوير**: a foot may run across a line break — the line's last word is then
  read in wasl (its final vowel not lengthened) and the foot completes in the
  next line. Marked ↵ in the report. Preserve pronounced sounds, including
  tanwin nun; distinguish semantic continuation from an actual divided foot.
- Line length is free; a one-foot line is fine.
- Rhyme is free; recurring end-sounds may still be pointed out as a strength.

## Checking a single line while composing
`python3 scripts/scan.py verify --meter kamil --free "السطر"`

# Shared-file Diwan CLI

Use the bundled `scripts/diwan.py` when the editor and agent can reach the same local computer. It uses Python's standard library; safe writes currently require macOS/Linux. Opening, saving and scanning need no model request or cloud publication. AI suggestions use the selected installed Claude/Codex client's existing login and usage allowance; no separate API key is required. Commands never prompt. Help is offline and has no setup side effects.

## One authoritative poem

The canonical `.diwan.json` file contains the title, exact UTF-8 poem text, review choices, suggestions, status, layout, meter, stable id, increasing revision and save identity. Both CLI and editor read/write this document. Browser storage is not the poem store in this mode. Hidden `.diwan/shared/` files contain immutable history, save receipts and local session state, not a competing current poem.

Import `.txt` or `.md` with `create --text-file`. Their complete contents are literal poem text; Markdown headings/frontmatter are not parsed or stripped. The original import file remains unchanged and is no longer the live draft. Export `txt`/`md` to obtain plain poem text again. Do not treat an old import/export as the latest shared document.

Run from the installed skill directory, or replace the script path with its absolute installed location:

```sh
python3 scripts/diwan.py --help
python3 scripts/diwan.py agent-context --command update --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py create /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --title نافذة --text-file /absolute/poems/draft.txt --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py open /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --agent auto --no-browser --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py get /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --json
```

Create the parent poem directory first. Use the current complete new/revised draft as input. Repeating create at the same path with the same initial fields returns the existing document; different content is a conflict, not permission to overwrite it. Preserve unrelated originals and use a separate canonical proposal when the poet has not accepted a revision.

`open` starts or reuses an owned loopback server and returns its exact URL. With `--no-browser`, open that URL through the agent's real browser capability and verify the visible poem. Without it, the CLI asks the operating system to open the browser; `browser_open_requested` is a request, not proof of rendered display. A display failure can leave a working server: use its returned URL rather than recreating the poem. `serve` runs in the foreground; `stop FILE` stops the owned server without changing the poem. Reopening reuses a healthy session. The editor is for one shared document; create/open another file for another poem.

If the current host cannot reach the same loopback server, state that limitation. A [preloaded snapshot](DIWAN.md#open-with-the-current-poem) remains available for local HTML viewers, but its browser edits do not synchronize to the canonical file. Do not promise shared-file behavior for that fallback.

## Conditional saving and recovery

Read `get --json` immediately before preparing an accepted save. Its `version` is an opaque content hash; `poem.revision` is the human-readable revision number. Write a JSON patch containing only intended editable fields, or use `--text-file` for an exact text-only update. `--input -` and `--text-file -` read stdin; empty input fails promptly.

```sh
python3 scripts/diwan.py update /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --input /absolute/poems/change.json --if-version CURRENT_VERSION --request-id edit-window-1 --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py history /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --limit 20 --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py restore /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --revision OLD_VERSION --if-version CURRENT_VERSION --request-id restore-window-1 --json
```

Replace version placeholders with actual `get`/`history` results. Reuse the same request id, patch and expected version when retrying the same uncertain save. Reusing an id with different input fails. Receipts recover a write interrupted after the canonical file changed. A replay reports both the originally applied version and the current document; it does not roll back later edits. A restore creates a new revision and retains intervening history. History defaults to 20 entries, supports `--before NEXT_CURSOR`, and never silently deletes older versions.

On `CONFLICT`, preserve the newer file and your proposed draft. Reread, compare and reassess; never silently substitute a fresh version for the stale patch. The editor keeps a conflicting draft visible, offers a download, and requires an explicit discard/reload to take the saved version. It warns before leaving with unsaved edits. It does not automatically merge simultaneous changes.

All supported writers use the same advisory file lock and conditional check, followed by an atomic complete-file replacement. Version history is durable before replacement. This prevents stale CLI/browser writes and torn saves between cooperating clients. A tool directly overwriting JSON outside this API ignores that lock and is unsupported; agents must use `update`, not a raw file write. Directory/file I/O failures can leave a committed save with an incomplete receipt: inspect `get` and retry the same operation identity, not a new create.

Create, update, restore, open and export accept `--dry-run`. A preview validates inputs without changing files, reserving a version or starting a browser/server. No delete command is provided. History and receipts are keyed by the stable poem id, while a directory-wide lock also covers case and Unicode filename aliases on macOS. Different files with a copied id in one workspace are rejected; import a new document instead. Renaming within the same directory retains history; `open` shuts down the old session and starts one at the new path, and `stop` can stop it directly. Stop the session before moving a poem to another directory or moving its workspace. Keep the canonical file and its .diwan history together when moving a workspace. Moving only the poem retains current content, not history in its former directory. There is no dedicated migration command. If shutdown cannot be confirmed, keep the session receipt and retry `stop` or `open`.

## Scan, export and existing chat

```sh
python3 scripts/diwan.py scan /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py export /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --format docx --output /absolute/poems/window.docx --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py pending /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --limit 20 --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py respond /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --id REQUEST_ID --input /absolute/poems/answer.json --json
```

Scanning uses Firas F. Khabour's existing local engine; interpret pronunciation/rules through [SCANNER.md](SCANNER.md). Export supports `txt`, literal `md`, and `docx`; Word uses the existing Node exporter. Existing identical output is reused. Different output needs another filename or explicit `--overwrite`. Generation happens in a temporary directory; final delivery is atomic and returns path/hash/bytes/source version. No PDF capability is added here.

Right-click a poem word, or use a two-finger click on a Mac trackpad, to open its replacement menu. A normal click edits spelling and vowels. Opening the replacement menu requests suggestions automatically when AI is connected; selecting a suggested replacement saves through the shared-file version guard. Failed requests show an error and a retry choice rather than leaving a spinner running.

New `open` and `serve` sessions detect a client automatically: prefer Claude when launched inside Claude Code, otherwise Codex if installed, then Claude. Reopening a running session preserves its current client unless `--agent` is explicit. Choose `--agent claude` or `--agent codex` when selecting that agent; the returned receipt names the actual client. An explicit change replaces the owned server at its existing port without changing the poem. Each AI action is a separate bounded model request through that client's saved login, not a turn in the existing conversation. It receives the bundled skill guidance and current poem/diagnostics, runs without shell/MCP access, and cannot save the poem. Calls use isolated client settings and low reasoning effort for interactive suggestions, keep no persistent chat session, time out after two minutes, and never retry or switch providers silently. The browser still checks suggested text against the current draft and scanner before applying it. A supplied host AI connection takes precedence without moving shared-file storage to a hosted database.

Use `--agent manual` to require the existing conversation instead. If neither client is installed, `auto` selects this fallback. Its dialog asks the poet to tell their chat to handle the request. Read bounded `pending` results, use the poetry skill, and `respond` with the required JSON. Cancellation stops an automatic client process; manual cancelled/expired requests cannot accept a response. A queued answer alone does not save a poem.

Results are JSON on stdout; errors are JSON on stderr. Exit codes: 0 success, 2 invalid input, 4 missing file/version, 5 conflict, 6 I/O, unsupported platform or delivery uncertainty. A nonzero exit does not prove that a preceding save or server launch was rolled back. Structured discovery describes the current flags, mutual exclusions and conditional capabilities. Profiles and remote-job controls are not applicable to this local, explicitly addressed workflow.
# Diwan editor and export

Diwan is the drafting and editing workbench contributed by Firas F. Khabour. Open it automatically when composing, continuing or revising a poem, once the complete draft is ready, using the local workflow below. Explicit chat-only, no-editor and poem-only delivery constraints take precedence. Quick analysis, close reading, critique without a rewrite and requested review-first pauses stay in chat. Use it for explicit editor, collection and export requests too. Read the [scanner workflow](SCANNER.md) for metrical claims and follow the main skill's vocalization policy.

## Open with the current poem

Prefer the [shared-file CLI](CLI.md) when the agent and browser can use the same local server. Its canonical `.diwan.json` document is the current poem for both participants, with guarded saves and history. The following preloaded-HTML procedure is a compatibility fallback for hosts with only a local HTML viewer. It copies the poem; browser changes in that fallback do not update a source file.

A composition, continuation or revision request authorizes the private local launch unless the poet opts out. An explicit editor request such as "open Diwan" or «افتح الديوان بهذه القصيدة» also triggers it. Complete the launch in the same turn without another offer or a request to paste text already available. For a new poem, preload the actual generated draft. For revision, preserve the original separately and preload the complete revised draft, including unchanged text, marks and line breaks. Keep proposals in review status; opening them is not acceptance. If an existing editor has unreadable newer edits, obtain that text through a real available capability before replacing anything.

1. Save the complete draft as UTF-8 text in a writable poem workspace outside the installed skill. For revision, keep the supplied source file unchanged and write the revised text to a separate draft file such as `draft.txt`. A request to revise the poem "in current.txt" identifies its input; it does not by itself request overwriting the file. Save back only when the poet accepts the revision or explicitly says to overwrite/save it to that source path. Choose a stable poem ID and reuse it when reopening that poem. Give unrelated poems different IDs.
2. Run the installed helper with real absolute paths. This example assumes the command runs from the installed skill directory:

   ```sh
   python3 scripts/prepare_diwan.py --poem /absolute/path/to/poems/current.txt --workspace /absolute/path/to/poems --id current-poem --title "عنوان القصيدة"
   ```

3. Open the returned `path` or `url` with the host's actual local HTML viewer or browser capability. Reuse and reload the existing Diwan tab for this workspace when one is open. Do not leave a second copy editing the same browser collection: local storage is not a multi-tab synchronization service, and an old tab can overwrite another tab's changes. Inspect the rendered title and poem to confirm delivery. The helper returns `opened: false`; creating the file alone is not opening it. If preview fails, use another available local viewer/browser or give the prepared file as an explicit remaining handoff. Never report an unrendered file as an open working editor.
4. Keep this launch local/private. Do not invoke hosted artifact publishing, deployment, shared databases or model services to open it. If the host only offers publishing, state that local display is unavailable and deliver the preloaded file through an available file tool. Do not ask the poet to copy the poem into an empty page.

The helper reuses the shipped HTML without rebuilding or modifying the installed package. It embeds the poem safely as data in a private file. The new entry starts in `review` status. The helper namespaces identity by workspace, poem ID and supplied text revision. Reopening the same supplied revision preserves its browser edits. If chat supplies a different revision, it opens as a separate review draft while the previous browser draft remains available. Visible notes distinguish the saved draft from a new supplied revision without guessing which is newer. If browser storage is unavailable, the poem still opens in memory with a warning to export before closing. Prepared HTML contains the poem and lives under `.diwan/`, with an ignore file for ordinary Git operations. Do not force-add poem data or assume this untracks files already committed. Prepared local copies do not request a hosted database. Their AI controls preserve an available host connection, otherwise use the local bridge below when attached or the manual exchange. Opening a poem does not prove the AI connection works.

## Choose an actually available environment

- `assets/workbench/diwan.html` is the built page. Its local scanner needs no AI call. It supports word/line edits, tashkeel choices, live feet and candidate meters, and collection export controls.
- An ordinary browser uses that browser's local storage. It does not synchronize with the agent, another browser or a later conversation. Keep local file locations and browser storage distinct.
- In the [shared-file CLI](CLI.md), AI controls use the selected installed Claude/Codex client automatically. A connected host may supply its own model service. An ordinary HTML viewer without either connection uses the manual request/response dialog. The status beside the toolbar identifies the selected client or fallback.
- Connected hosts may supply AI, database and download capabilities through the adapter described below. Claude host support remains optional. Shared poem storage requires an actual database capability; otherwise poems stay in browser storage.
- Word download uses a connected host when available and an ordinary browser download otherwise. Fonts and JSZip still load from CDNs; the page is not fully offline. If browser download is unavailable, use the CLI exporter.
- Never invent Artifact, ArtifactData, SendUserFile, publish, database or download APIs. Use the real tools and schemas supplied by the environment. Opening a local page, saving a local file, and publishing an externally accessible artifact are different actions; follow the user's scope.

Preserve the page footer credit, "Compliments from Firas F. Khabour & Daniel Petro · Oct. 2026", when copying or rebuilding. Preserve `assets/fonts/OFL.txt` with the bundled Amiri fonts.

## Guide the poet through review

When Diwan is used, keep chat guidance short and point the poet to the actual opened page or file. Explain the relevant controls rather than dumping the raw scanner report:

- Amber shading marks proposed tashkeel choices, dotted underlining marks missing tashkeel, and red marks words inside a broken foot. Click a word to choose a reading, set its final mark, or enter another form. Right-click it, or two-finger click on a Mac trackpad, for synonyms, words with the same rhythm, or meaning-preserving replacements that repair meter. Connected AI requests these automatically; manual mode waits for an explicit menu choice. Explain only the actual choices for this poem.
- The poet can edit a line or the whole poem. Scansion updates locally: foot blocks show the name, syllable pattern and عروض letters; green/red blocks and line diagnoses locate the match or mismatch. Ordinary editing/scanning does not require an AI request.
- Use the layout buttons for automatic detection, one بيت per line, paired hemistich lines or taf‘ila. The meter selector and candidate meters let the poet test another reading; returning to automatic mode clears the manual selection.
- A line conversation discusses the current line. Where the connected assistant supports `check_lines`, it verifies suggestions through the page's scanner. A scanner pass still needs grammar, rhyme and meaning review.
- «بدائل لتقويم الوزن» offers checked alternatives and a replacement control. A proposed alternative is not permission to replace the poet's line; explain its meaning tradeoff and let the poet choose.
- «اعتمد التشكيل» records the poet's approval. Keep `status: "review"` until that action or an explicit instruction to approve. On returning to the chat, read the latest stored or supplied text and scan that accepted reading; never continue from the stale pre-review copy.
- The poem menu switches poems and provides confirmed deletion; «+ قصيدة» opens a composer. Copy/export controls apply to the selected poem or collection. Confirm the actual current text/order before exporting, and preserve the source collection when preparing an output file.

If the environment has no readable host store, do not claim to read browser-local edits. Ask for the current text or exported data through an available route. For a host tool that exposes `version`/`if_version`, read the current version and use its documented conditional-write field; otherwise follow that host's actual concurrency contract.

## Local workflow

Reuse the shipped HTML for ordinary use; copy it into the output workspace if needed. Open it only through an available browser/file-opening capability, or provide the real file path. Do not claim it opened when no such capability exists.

The local scanner, Word exporter and font assets stay together inside the installed skill. For source changes, rebuild with `python3 scripts/build_workbench.py`; this rewrites the installed meter JSON and HTML, so it is a maintainer operation rather than a requirement for every poem. Run it in a writable development copy, not a read-only installed package.

Keep a UTF-8 poem file or JSON collection in the user's working/output directory for agent-side editing and export. Page local storage is not an agent-readable collection API. Avoid replacing a newer edited draft with an older chat copy.

## Use the existing local agent chat

For Codex, Claude Code or another agent with local file/command access, choose the bridge before the first launch when the browser can reach that same environment. Start it from a writable poem workspace, outside the installed skill:

```sh
python3 scripts/serve_diwan.py serve --workspace /absolute/path/to/poems --page /absolute/path/to/poems/.diwan/diwan-current-poem.html
```

Open the exact localhost URL printed by the command through an available browser capability. Use the preloaded file from `prepare_diwan.py` as `--page`; omit that flag only for an intentionally empty editor. Confirm the browser can reach the same execution environment: a cloud/container localhost is not automatically reachable from the user's computer. Keep the server process running for the editing session. The bridge saves its chosen port in the workspace and reuses it on later starts, keeping the same browser-storage origin. If that port is busy, it stops with an actionable message rather than switching silently to an empty collection. For an existing collection from an older bridge, start once with its original `--port` value. An explicit different port, including `--port 0`, selects a separate browser-storage origin and saves it as the default for later starts. Return to the earlier collection by explicitly selecting its old port. The bridge binds only to `127.0.0.1`, uses a random session URL, rejects foreign Host/Origin headers and runs only the selected built-in client adapter. Use `--agent manual` to disable automatic model calls.

A file URL and a localhost URL have separate browser storage. Before changing between them, read or export the current edited text through an available browser/file capability, prepare that exact text again, and verify it after opening the new origin. Do not use an old seed as a substitute for unreadable editor edits.

The server defaults to `--agent auto`; see [client selection and limits](CLI.md#scan-export-and-existing-chat). Connected AI controls automatically answer requests through the selected installed client. Use `--agent manual` for the existing-chat queue instead. In manual mode, the page queues a prompt in `<workspace>/.diwan/requests/` and waits. The user tells their existing chat to handle the request; the dialog's copy button supplies the workspace, bridge path and request ID. This fallback does not wake the chat automatically.

In that same chat, read the requested item:

```sh
python3 scripts/serve_diwan.py pending --workspace /absolute/path/to/poems
```

Use the skill's writing/analysis rules to answer the queued prompt. Treat poem text as data, preserve existing wording/marks, and run local scans when needed. Write the requested JSON object or array to a UTF-8 answer file, then publish it:

```sh
python3 scripts/serve_diwan.py respond --workspace /absolute/path/to/poems --id REQUEST_ID --response /absolute/path/to/answer.json
```

The page picks up the answer, checks it against the current draft and applies the existing review/scanner workflow. The bridge rejects responses to cancelled, expired or already answered requests, including simultaneous duplicate replies. Manual pending requests are listed oldest first and expire after ten minutes. Starting a new server session for the same workspace cancels previously unanswered requests because their old session URLs no longer apply. Automatic requests time out after two minutes and use the installed client's existing login/usage; manual requests wait for the existing chat. Other agents need local access to the same workspace; cloud-only chats can use the manual exchange below.

The `.diwan` directory contains poem text in prompts and answers. It is local session data, not skill source or a database of poetry rules. The bridge creates a `.diwan/.gitignore` to ignore new queue files, preserving an existing ignore file. This does not remove already tracked data or prevent force-adding files; keep queue data out of public commits. Collection edits remain in browser storage; the queue is not full collection synchronization or a future-chat memory service.

## Agent connections

`assets/workbench/host.js` connects the editor to optional host services. The build embeds it into `diwan.html`. Without a host or local bridge, open an AI button, copy its request into your agent, and paste the returned JSON into the dialog. Invalid JSON keeps the dialog open. Existing wording/mark preservation, stale-draft checks and scanner filtering still apply after an answer arrives. A browser-scanned suggestion remains provisional evidence, not a guarantee of linguistic validity.

For a connected integration, supply `window.DiwanHost` before the application boots:

```js
window.DiwanHost = {
  label: 'My agent',
  sample: {
    async limits() { return { tools: false }; },
    async json(input, options) { /* return a parsed JSON answer */ }
  }
};
```

This is an adapter contract, not a working model connection by itself. `input` is either a prompt string or an array of `{role, content}` turns. Set `sample.requiresUserHandoff: true` if a request needs a user dialog or chat handoff; word menus then wait for an explicit AI choice before requesting suggestions. Honor `options.signal` cancellation. Advertise `tools: true` only if the adapter actually supports `options.tools`, including executing each supplied tool callback and returning its result to the model. Otherwise the page verifies proposed lines after receiving the response.

Optional `db` and `downloads` properties use the existing collection/document and `save({filename, data})` contracts below. Ordinary browsers use local storage, native downloads and the manual request dialog. A Claude host with no granted downloads capability keeps its original unavailable-download message; do not assume its sandbox permits native blob downloads. An injected host may set `downloads: null` to disable downloads explicitly; an omitted field uses the ordinary-browser fallback. An adapter must implement its provider's real authentication and permission requirements outside the poem UI. Never put provider secrets in shipped HTML. Do not claim an agent connection merely because an adapter name is shown.

Codex's [App Server documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex/app-server/) describes an integration for conversations, approvals and streamed events. This package uses the local file queue above for existing chats, not an automatic Codex App Server adapter. Its queue and portable request dialog require no separate API key or agent run. Agents need access to the skill and local execution to run the Python scanner; the browser scanner works independently.

## Compatible hosted workflow

Only if actual host tools expose these capabilities, look for the poet's existing workbench titled «ديوان العروض» and reuse it rather than creating duplicates. The original contribution uses Artifact/ArtifactData names; treat the following as its data contract, not proof that the current host supports those tools.

For the original fully connected workflow, host capability declarations historically included database, sampling and downloads, `{"db": {}, "sample": {}, "downloads": {}}`. Request/use only real granted capabilities: the database enables shared collection storage, sampling enables AI buttons and downloads enables host file delivery. Use the documented fallback or unavailable state for each missing capability.

The collection is `poems`, one document per poem with a short stable ID:

```json
{
  "title": "عنوان",
  "text": "النص المشكول، سطر في كل سطر، والشطران بينهما *",
  "status": "review",
  "mode": "auto",
  "meter": "",
  "order": 0,
  "choices": [{"line": 1, "word": "كلمة", "note": "موضع القراءة", "options": [{"text": "كَلِمَة", "note": "القراءة"}], "done": false}],
  "suggestions": {"1": [{"text": "بديل محقق", "note": "أثره في المعنى"}]}
}
```

Use the host's actual concurrency/version mechanism when updating an existing document. Read before writing, preserve user edits, and read back the current text before analyzing after an editing session. `status: "confirmed"` records the page's approval action; do not set it on the poet's behalf during a requested review-first step. Choices are 1-based line references; put the proposed reading first in each options list and keep undecided choices open for the poet. Keep only verified suggestions and explain semantic tradeoffs.

The page supports poem selection, local/host storage, line conversations when sampling exists, approved tashkeel choices, mode/meter controls and export. Use actual host evidence before saying a poem is saved across conversations or that a file was delivered.

## Word, text and optional PDF

CLI Word export uses Python plus Node.js, not the browser's host-download capability. Prepare a JSON list in the stored `order` sequence, or the order explicitly requested by the poet, each item containing `title`, `text`, `mode` and `meter`. Read the actual host collection if one is available; otherwise use the user's provided text or current local working copy.

```sh
python3 scripts/export_book.py poems.json out.docx --appendix --text out.txt
python3 scripts/export_book.py poems.json out.docx --tashkeel light --title "ديواني"
python3 scripts/export_book.py poems.json out.docx --layout table
python3 scripts/export_book.py poems.json out.docx --pdf
```

Options include `--tashkeel full|light|none`, a title page, a scansion appendix, and `--layout paras|table` for copy-friendly paragraphs or fixed columns. The classical layout places صدر right and عجز left. Plain text separates halves with five spaces. Report the actual generated file paths and deliver them through a real available file capability.

PDF additionally needs LibreOffice (`soffice`), font support and `fc-cache`. The current `--pdf` path can copy bundled Amiri fonts into `~/.fonts` and refresh the cache. Check the environment and authorization before that global filesystem change; otherwise deliver Word/text and state the missing PDF requirement. A successful DOCX export does not prove PDF conversion or host download integration.

    assert z.testzip() is None
    root=ET.fromstring(z.read('word/document.xml'))
    text=''.join(root.itertext())
    assert 'مسافة' in text
    assert 'قَرِيبٌ صَدِيقِي بَعِيدٌ مَكَانِي' in text
print('Verified DOCX archive, title, and exact vocalized poem text.')
